title: Prefetch large hosted standalone Uniform shuffle input
question: Can a single bounded speculative read improve complete hosted Uniform Runs with the same engine, spill plan and output verification?
summary: All eleven eligible pairs improved. The 1.265 GB Chrome OPFS case saved 3.119 seconds at the paired median. Chrome's local disk File held-out case saved 1.896 seconds.

workloads: Hosted Run receiving one explicit Uniform shuffle, selected .csv of at least 128 MiB and plain output.
Persistent Chrome File and OPFS sources, fixed 64 to 256 MiB and the same feature-free WASM in both arms.

validation.summary: All complete jobs verify row fields, membership, CSV caps, marker readback and retirement. Output jobs below the size floor use synchronous reads. Injected source rejection falls back, cancellation retires with a source read unresolved, and malformed input fails cleanly.

limitations: Single WSL2 ext4 host, synthetic fixtures, uncontrolled caches and OPFS destinations.
One existing 256 KiB pending source read uses the documented 2.5 MiB plus 24 control bytes streaming capacity outside the WASI reservations.
exclusions: Multi-operation, compressed-output or non-Uniform jobs and native performance.
reopen_when: A representative eligible source shows a repeated complete-Run regression or a buffer lifetime regression.
